name: Natural House Aoyama
who: Japan's original organic supermarket chain (about 30 stores nationwide), anchored by its Aoyama store near Omotesando.
why: The store that brought organic and macrobiotic groceries into mainstream Tokyo shopping.
takeaway: Go for the store that first brought organic and macrobiotic groceries into mainstream Tokyo shopping.

name: Crayon House
who: Organic cafe, grocery and bookstore in Aoyama, open since 1976 as a combined publishing house and health-food pioneer.
why: One of Tokyo's oldest organic institutions, still open and still mixing books, toys and organic food under one roof.
takeaway: Go for the odd mix — organic groceries, a bookstore and toys under one Aoyama roof since 1976.

name: Hansalim
who: South Korea's largest organic consumer cooperative, founded in 1986, with retail shops across Seoul serving well over a million members.
why: Defined the direct farmer-to-consumer organic movement in Korea; the world's biggest cooperative of its kind.
takeaway: Go to see the world's biggest organic consumer co-op in action — direct farmer-to-consumer buying, not a boutique shop.

name: Chorokmaeul (Green Village)
who: Organic co-op supermarket chain with stores across Korea, a sister strand of the country's farm-to-table cooperative movement.
why: A flagship of Korea's organic co-op retail scene, distinct from Hansalim's larger cooperative model.
takeaway: Go to see Korea's organic co-op retail scene from a different angle than the bigger Hansalim model.

name: Orga Whole Foods
who: Premium organic grocery chain in Seoul known for imported and domestic organic goods with in-store cafe corners.
why: Seoul's closest equivalent to a Western-style organic supermarket experience.
takeaway: Go for the closest thing Seoul has to a Western-style organic supermarket experience, cafe corner included.

name: Green Common
who: Hong Kong's leading plant-based grocery-and-cafe flagship, a two-storey concept in Central with a grocery, deli and restaurant.
why: The regional reference for plant-based retail, backed by the Green Monday movement.
takeaway: Go for the region's reference plant-based grocery-deli-restaurant concept, two storeys deep in Central.

name: Little Farms
who: Singapore's premium organic and health-food grocer chain, multiple locations descending from its original Dempsey Hill store.
why: The default organic grocer for Singapore's health-conscious expat and local shoppers.
takeaway: Go for the default organic grocer of Singapore's health-conscious expat and local shopping crowd.

name: SuperNature
who: Independent organic and health-food store with a cafe corner, a longstanding name in Singapore's wellness retail scene.
why: One of Singapore's older organic specialty grocers, known for curated imported goods.
takeaway: Go for curated imported goods at one of Singapore's older organic specialty grocers, cafe corner included.

name: Lemon Farm
who: Thailand's pioneering organic supermarket chain, founded 1999 and now 14-plus branches with in-store organic cafes.
why: Defined organic retail in Thailand and helped build the country's organic-farmer supply network.
takeaway: Go for the chain that defined organic retail in Thailand and built its farmer supply network.

name: Nature's Basket
who: India's premium gourmet-and-organic grocery chain, active with a rebuilt flagship store in Mumbai's Khar area.
why: The reference for curated imported and organic goods in urban India, though closer to gourmet than pure health-food.
takeaway: Go for curated imported and organic goods — more gourmet than pure health-food, but the urban-India reference.

name: The Source Bulk Foods
who: Originator of Australia's zero-waste bulk-foods grocery format, founded 2012 near Byron Bay, now 50-plus stores including overseas expansion.
why: Created the bring-your-own-container, buy-by-weight retail model now copied worldwide.
takeaway: Go to see the bring-your-own-container, buy-by-weight model Australia's zero-waste grocers everywhere have since copied.

name: Flannerys
who: Queensland-founded organic and health-food supermarket chain with stores across QLD and northern NSW.
why: A long-running regional institution for organic groceries and supplements in southeast Queensland.
takeaway: Go for a long-running regional institution stocking organic groceries and supplements across southeast Queensland.

name: Terra Madre
who: Independent organic grocer and cafe in Melbourne known for its curated pantry and produce selection.
why: A neighborhood fixture for Melbourne's organic and slow-food crowd.
takeaway: Go for a curated pantry — a neighborhood fixture for Melbourne's organic and slow-food crowd.

name: Wholefoods House
who: Independent health-food store in Sydney offering organic groceries, supplements and bulk goods.
why: A steady, no-frills fixture of Sydney's health-food retail scene.
takeaway: Go for a steady, no-frills fixture of Sydney's health-food retail scene — groceries, supplements, bulk goods.

name: Commonsense Organics
who: Independent organic supermarket group founded in the 1990s, with anchor stores in Wellington's Thorndon and Newtown.
why: A defining institution of New Zealand's organic-food retail culture.
takeaway: Go for a defining piece of New Zealand's organic-food retail culture, anchored in two Wellington neighborhoods.

name: Mundo Verde
who: Brazil's organic and health-food supermarket chain, founded in the late 1990s with stores across Sao Paulo.
why: Brazil's reference organic supermarket brand, credited with popularizing organic retail nationally.
takeaway: Go for the chain credited with popularizing organic retail across Brazil, since the late 1990s.

name: The Green Corner
who: Organic and health-food grocery chain in Mexico City with a cafe and juice-bar format across several branches.
why: One of Mexico City's go-to spots for organic groceries and a health-food lifestyle scene.
takeaway: Go for the juice bar and cafe that make this a go-to for Mexico City's health-food scene.

name: Organic Foods & Cafe
who: The Middle East's pioneering organic supermarket and cafe, founded 2004, with locations across Dubai.
why: Introduced organic retail to the Gulf region and remains its most established organic grocer.
takeaway: Go for the store that introduced organic retail to the Gulf and remains its most established name.

name: Wellness Warehouse
who: South Africa's leading wellness-and-organic retail chain, flagship on Cape Town's Kloof Street, with stores nationwide.
why: Defined organic and supplement retail in South Africa, closest thing the country has to a health-food department store.
takeaway: Go for South Africa's closest thing to a health-food department store — organic groceries plus a full supplement wall.

name: Jackson's Real Food Market
who: Independent organic and real-food grocery and cafe in Johannesburg's Craighall Park.
why: A community favorite for organic produce and clean-eating groceries in Joburg's northern suburbs.
takeaway: Go for organic produce and clean-eating groceries, a community favorite in Joburg's northern suburbs.
